# Stories To Watch

> An independent luxury-watch discovery house: cinematic stories on the world's most storied watches, real market prices, and where to buy from 75 verified dealers worldwide. We don't review watches — we tell the stories behind them, then help you find and value the real thing. Founded 2026. Independent; sources checked, never bought.

## Featured stories
- [Lord Shiva on the Wrist — Jacob & Co. Epic X Mahadev Edition](https://www.storiestowatch.com/jacob-co-mahadev-shiva-watch.html): Jacob & Co. unveiled the Epic X Mahadev Edition on 16 September 2026 — its first watch built around Lord Shiva. A 44mm titanium skeleton on the Epic X platform, its openworked dial carries the figure of Shiva with the trishul (trident), damru (drum) and Om, and the mantra "Om Namah Shivaya" at six o'clock, all glowing in blue Super-LumiNova after dark. Movement: hand-wound JCAM02 skeleton calibre, 28,800 vph, 48-hour power reserve. Sold exclusively through Ethos Watches in India; no official global price published (Indian coverage reported ~₹35.88 lakh, indicative only). A clear example of the 2026 shift toward story-first, culturally specific grails.
- [The $3.4 Million Quartz Watch — Cartier's Cheich](https://www.storiestowatch.com/cartier-cheich-record.html): A unique white-gold Cartier Cheich sold for HK$26.52M (~US$3.4M with fees) at Sotheby's Important Watches sale in Hong Kong on 18 September 2026 — the most valuable Cartier wristwatch ever sold at auction, and the most valuable quartz watch ever sold. It beat the previous Cartier record, a 1987 London Crash (~US$2M, Sotheby's 2026). The Cheich was created in 1983 as the trophy for "The Cartier Challenge" at the Paris-Dakar Rally (its name is the indigo Tuareg headscarf); only a handful exist and this is the sole white-gold example, commissioned 2010. Signals that in 2026 the market pays for rarity, provenance, shape and story over movement type — mechanical or quartz.
- [Australia's Most Expensive Watch Is One Nobody Could Buy](https://www.storiestowatch.com/rolex-daytona-rainbow-auction-record.html): A gem-set Rolex Cosmograph Daytona "Rainbow" (Ref. 126598RBOW) — allocation-only and near-impossible to buy at retail — sold for AU$612,000 through First State Auctions in Sydney in July 2026, the most expensive watch ever sold at auction in Australia (hammer AU$510,000 + 20% premium). It cleared the previous national record of AU$450,000 (a 1946 Patek Philippe ref. 1436, 2023) — and the collector who set that old record is the same anonymous Australian tech founder who consigned the Rainbow. It was also the first example of the reference offered at auction anywhere in the world. Retail ~AU$324,700. All figures in Australian dollars.
- [The First Watch on the Moon Is Lost](https://www.storiestowatch.com/first-watch-on-the-moon.html): Buzz Aldrin's Omega Speedmaster (ref. ST 105.012) was the first watch worn on the Moon during Apollo 11 on 21 July 1969, then lost in transit to the Smithsonian c.1971 and never recovered. In July 2026 his other watches sold at Sotheby's — his personal 1990 Speedmaster for ~$44,800 and the Apollo 11 pen and circuit-breaker switch for $857,600. Also covers the Apollo 13 14-second Speedmaster burn.
- [The Cartier Crash — the Accident That Never Happened](https://www.storiestowatch.com/cartier-crash-story.html): The melted-case Cartier Crash's famous 1967 car-crash origin story is almost certainly a myth; it was a deliberate Cartier London design. A circa-1987 example sold for ~$2 million at Sotheby's in April 2026.
- [The Wrist of Champions](https://www.storiestowatch.com/wrist-of-champions.html): Reading winners — athletes, managers, icons — through the watches they choose.

## Guides & comparisons
- [The 2026 Watch Market Split in Two](https://www.storiestowatch.com/2026-watch-market-split.html): The 2026 luxury-watch market has normalised from the 2021–22 peak and split WITHIN brands, not between them — a Patek Nautilus trades ~74% over retail while a Patek Calatrava sits ~34% below. Which references are rising (hyped steel sports, independents like F.P. Journe), which are softening (dress and out-of-hype tool watches), and how to buy well — with Morgan Stanley / WatchCharts data.
- [Royal Oak vs Nautilus vs Daytona — Which Grail Holds Value in 2026?](https://www.storiestowatch.com/royal-oak-vs-nautilus-vs-daytona.html): The three steel grails compared for 2026 — the Patek Nautilus wins on store-of-value, the AP Royal Oak on design, the Rolex Daytona on liquidity and daily wear. Real secondary-market prices (USD) and which one suits which buyer.
- [Audemars Piguet Royal Oak Price Guide 2026](https://www.storiestowatch.com/royal-oak-price-guide.html): Every major Royal Oak reference valued at current 2026 market prices, where to source, and which references hold value best.
- [Patek Philippe vs Rolex — Which Holds Value in 2026?](https://www.storiestowatch.com/patek-vs-rolex-investment-2026.html): How Rolex and Patek Philippe behave in the secondary market — Rolex on liquidity, Patek on multiples — with the actual 2026 numbers.

## Tools
- [Watch Finder](https://www.storiestowatch.com/watchfinder.html): Find where to buy a specific luxury watch from verified dealers worldwide.
- [Fair Value](https://www.storiestowatch.com/fair-value.html): What a given watch is really worth at current market prices.
- [Availability Check](https://www.storiestowatch.com/availability-check.html): A flat-fee ($45) market check for serious buyers — whether a specific watch is realistically available now, the best route (retail, pre-owned, grey market or auction), a realistic timeline, and the alternatives worth considering. The first paid step before full sourcing.
- [Source a Watch (concierge)](https://www.storiestowatch.com/source-a-watch.html): Can't find it? Our buyer-side concierge assesses what's realistic and sources the exact reference through trusted channels. You buy direct; we never hold the watch or your money.
